result:
The retention spec (`apps/web/e2e/p7-retention.spec.ts`) now passes on the real stack in both languages: 3 runs in a row with both projects in parallel, plus one run with chromium-ar first and then chromium-en. All exited 0. It's a test-only change; no product code was touched.

**What was wrong.** The test was failing for two reasons, one hidden behind the other:
1. **Language.** The two language projects run at the same time and both signed in as the seeded `dev.admin`, which has a single stored language preference. When the Arabic run switched language, the English page picked it up on its next load or in-app navigation. So it was a race on that shared setting, not a run-order problem. `signIn` already called `ensureLanguage`, so adding it alone would not have fixed this.
2. **Shared retention class.** Once the language was isolated, both projects reached the change form for the same class, `job_history`, at the same moment. Whichever saved second got the product's correct 409 "Someone else changed this record" screen. That failed English 3 out of 3 times; those logs are kept as `intermediate-…-run{1,2,3}.log`.

**What I changed in the spec:**
- **Own user per test and language.** Each test creates its own synthetic user through the real API, with its stored language set to that project's language and only the role under test (ADM_TECH or AUD). This is the same pattern `p5-navigation.spec.ts` uses. At the end the user's roles are revoked. The seeded `dev.admin` only creates and grants these users and no longer signs in to the browser here.
- **Language checked after every load.** `ensureLanguage` now runs after every full page load, and the language is checked again after the in-app jump from a class link.
- **Own class per language.** English edits `job_history` and Arabic edits `webhook_receipt_log`. The two have the same shape in migration 0143, and both stay on "Keep". All the original assertions are unchanged.

**Checks run (all exit 0):**

| Check | Exit |
|---|---|
| e2e, both projects in parallel, 3 runs | 0, 4 passed each time |
| e2e, ar first then en, on one stack | 0 |
| `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm openapi:lint` | 0 |
| `pnpm test` | 0 |
| prettier check over all files | 0 |
| `validate.mjs --historical --stage DG6` | 0 |

I didn't run any integration tests on a disposable PostgreSQL or the contract test, because no API or integration test changed. The e2e runs used the existing `apps/web/dist` and `apps/api/dist` builds without rebuilding them; that's fine for a test-only change.

**Known gaps:**
- Each run leaves 2 synthetic users per language, with their roles revoked. On the disposable test stack they disappear with the database, but on a long-lived stack they stay, because users can't be deleted.
- Several other specs (the p2–p5 journeys among them) still sign in as `dev.admin` in both languages at once, so the same race could make them flaky. I didn't change them because they're outside this task.

**Open question:** should the per-language user helper move into `support/ui.ts` so those other specs can use it? That would touch other owners' specs, so it's your call.

Nothing is committed. Files are in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG7/`:
- `T-DG7-FE-C3-frontend-ux-engineer.md` (the handback)
- `T-DG7-FE-C3-evidence/` (logs, plus screenshots of the saved class form: `p7-retention-class-saved-en.png`, `p7-retention-class-saved-ar.png`)
